introduction.en: Agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihood in India, employing nearly half the workforce while facing structural vulnerabilities like climate shocks, fragmented landholdings, and market volatility. Expert committees and commissions have historically served as institutional lighthouses, diagnosing these systemic challenges and prescribing comprehensive roadmaps for reform.
introduction.hi: Agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihood in India, employing nearly half the workforce while facing structural vulnerabilities like climate shocks, fragmented landholdings, and market volatility. Expert committees and commissions have historically served as institutional lighthouses, diagnosing these systemic challenges and prescribing comprehensive roadmaps for reform.

body.en:
The National Commission on Farmers (2004–2006), chaired by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, revolutionized agricultural discourse by advocating a paradigm shift from production-centric policies to farmers-centric welfare. Its landmark recommendation on pricing—setting MSP at 50% over the C2 comprehensive cost of production—remains a cornerstone of policy debates. Furthermore, the commission addressed vital socio-economic aspects such as land rights for women farmers, the establishment of a National Grain Reserve, and robust crop insurance mechanisms.

Building upon this, the Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income (2016) under Ashok Dalwai provided an operational framework anchored in seven distinct growth vectors. Moving beyond mere output augmentation, the committee stressed net income enhancement through enhanced resource use efficiency, reduction in cultivation costs, integration of allied sectors (dairying, horticulture, fisheries), value addition through food processing, and efficient post-harvest supply chain management linked with digital platforms like e-NAM.

In tandem, committees on agricultural credit (such as the B. Sivaraman Committee for NABARD and Vyas Committee for rural banking) restructured institutional credit delivery, helping reduce reliance on informal moneylenders. Similarly, task forces on agricultural marketing catalyzed the formulation of Model APMC Acts, paving the way for contract farming and private market participation.

Translating their holistic recommendations into actionable state and central interventions is essential for achieving climate-resilient agriculture, ensuring food security, and securing a prosperous future for Indian farmers.

overview.title: Committees Related To Agriculture
overview.definition: Agricultural committees in India comprise expert bodies, task forces, and parliamentary panels established to review agrarian distress, price policy, cooperative credit, marketing reforms, and sustainable farming, providing actionable roadmaps for policy formulation.
overview.importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC CSE Prelims (factual questions on committee chairpersons and landmark reports) and Mains GS Paper 3 (Agriculture: pricing, MSP, doubling farmers' income, credit, and supply chain reforms).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and historical evolution of agricultural committees and commissions in India.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, pricing policies, and structural reform dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions regarding committee mandates.

sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Evolution of Agricultural Committees**: Ranging from the **Royal Commission on Agriculture (1928)** under Lord Linlithgow to modern reform panels like the **Swaminathan Commission (2004)**, committees have shaped Indian agricultural policy.
• **Mandate and Scope**: Encompasses crop pricing, institutional credit, cooperative movement, agricultural marketing, biotechnology regulation, and climate-resilient agriculture.
• **Advisory vs. Statutory Nature**: Most agricultural committees are high-level expert groups or task forces submitting recommendations; implementation rests with the Union and State governments.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Integration of committee recommendations into the **Union Budget**, **Economic Survey**, and statutory amendments like the **Model APMC Act**.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Price Policy & MSP: M.S. Swaminathan Commission (NCF, 2004-06)
Recommended MSP at C2 cost + 50%; comprehensive land reforms; holistic agrarian distress management.
Addressing agrarian crisis, farmers' suicides, and ensuring remunerative pricing.
Frequent Prelims and Mains questions on C2 costs vs. A2+FL costs and MSP formulas.
Institutional Credit: R.V. Gupta Committee (1998) & T.K. Viswanathan / Nachiket Mor
Rationalization of interest rates, introduction of Kisan Credit Card (KCC), and expanding rural banking reach.
Enhancing credit flow to agriculture, reducing reliance on informal moneylenders.
Prelims source for the origin of Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme.
Marketing & Supply Chain: Ashok Dalwai Committee (2017)
Focused on 'Doubling Farmers' Income' (DFI) by 2022-23 through a 7-pillar strategy.
Balancing production growth with post-harvest management, value addition, and market linkages.
Extensively used in Mains GS-3 answers on agricultural marketing and farmers' income.

items.definition: Chaired by M.S. Swaminathan; landmark 5-report series proposing comprehensive agrarian reform, including women in agriculture and risk management.
A2+FL covers actual paid-out costs plus imputed value of family labor; C2 cost additionally includes imputed rent and interest on owned land and capital assets.

items.term: Shri C. Rangachari Committee / Task Force
items.definition: Associated with agricultural credit and cooperative sector revitalization, focusing on structural reforms in rural credit institutions.
Examined the working of the Forward Markets Commission and futures trading in agricultural commodities.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Green Revolution Belt (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP)**: Studied extensively by committees for groundwater depletion, stubble burning, and diversification.
• **Rainfed & Dryland Zones (Vidarbha, Marathwada, Rayalaseema)**: Focal regions for dryland farming committees, micro-irrigation task forces, and suicide-prevention packages.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Delays in committee report implementation, Centre-State legislative conflicts over Agri-marketing (List II, Entry 14).
• **Policy Interventions**: Adoption of Model APMC Acts, e-NAM integration, and promotion of Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) as recommended by various task forces.

items.title: Mnemonic for Major Agricultural Committees
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'S-A-R-V' (Swaminathan, Ashok Dalwai, R.V. Gupta, Vyas Committee).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Swaminathan (Farmers/MSP), Ashok Dalwai (Doubling Farmers Income), R.V. Gupta (Kisan Credit Card), Vyas (Rural Credit/Agricultural Indebtedness).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly matches committee names with their core domain during match-the-following MCQs.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Whenever a question mentions 'C2 Cost + 50%', immediately link it to the **Swaminathan Commission (NCF)**; whenever 'Kisan Credit Card (KCC)' is asked, link it to the **R.V. Gupta Committee**.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often creates statements claiming that the Government of India has legally accepted all recommendations of the Swaminathan Commission, including C2 + 50% MSP as a statutory right. This is incorrect; while MSP is announced, C2 + 50% as a mandatory legal guarantee has not been statutorily implemented.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 answers on agricultural distress or reform, quote the Ashok Dalwai Committee's 7-pillar strategy (focusing on productivity, resource use efficiency, post-harvest management, value addition, market reforms, risk management, and alternative livelihoods) to secure top marks.

keyTakeaways: Agricultural committees provide the foundational policy blueprints for pricing, credit, and structural reforms in India.
The M.S. Swaminathan Commission (NCF) and Ashok Dalwai Committee remain the most critical references for Mains enrichment.
Matching committee mandates with their specific institutional outcomes (e.g., R.V. Gupta for KCC) is a high-yield area for Prelims.

question.en: Discuss the major recommendations of the M.S. Swaminathan Commission (National Commission on Farmers) and evaluate their relevance in addressing contemporary agrarian distress in India.
question.hi: Discuss the major recommendations of the M.S. Swaminathan Commission (National Commission on Farmers) and evaluate their relevance in addressing contemporary agrarian distress in India.

modelAnswer.en:
Introduction: Briefly introduce the National Commission on Farmers (NCF) headed by Prof. M.S. Swaminathan established in 2004.
Body:
• Core Recommendations: MSP at C2 cost + 50% profit margin, land reforms, institutional credit access, assured irrigation, and safety nets for crop failure.
• Agrarian Crisis Context: Addressing rural indebtedness, farmers' suicides, and climate vulnerabilities.
• Evaluation/Relevance: While pricing is crucial, modern challenges require diversification, digital agriculture, supply-chain modernization, and climate-resilient farming as recommended by subsequent committees like Ashok Dalwai.
Conclusion: Emphasize a holistic policy framework combining remunerative prices with structural transformation for sustainable agricultural growth.
